items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — went straight from the greeting into asking for her name
No agenda statement ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, sound good?') before diving into probing questions
Never asked about narrow hallways/tight turns or walk distance from truck to door beyond confirming the driveway and lack of steps
Never asked whether Lina needed packing help — a real miss given she said 'I have to hire, to hire help to get the rest of the stuff'
Never asked a moving-stressors question ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Meet Your Mover (photo + basic info emailed before move day) never mentioned
No packing service pricing offered despite Lina's stated need for help finishing packing before move day
No relatable size equivalent (e.g., school-bus load) used to frame the estimate
Save Your Ass speech covered consolidation examples but skipped the 'take a carload' tip for small items she can move herself
Never asked 'Any other questions before I let you go?' before ending the call
No office hours or way to reach the branch given beyond the call itself
Used Lina's name only once at the very start ('L-E-N-A you said') and relied on 'ma'am' for the rest of the 16.7-minute call, well under the 3+ bar
No rapport-building or humor moment — call stayed strictly transactional start to finish
No 60¢/lb baseline insurance alternative mentioned alongside the No Worries $2,000 coverage
top_strength: Rance gave a transparent, well-organized hourly-pricing breakdown and deliberately erred conservative on the time estimate ('I'd rather be a little bit more conservative with my estimate and kind of give you good news at the end of the day'), which built trust and matched Lina's minimal-inventory situation.
coaching_note: When Lina said she needs to 'hire help to get the rest of the stuff' packed, Rance should have pivoted straight into pricing packing services — instead he moved on to the next probing question and never revisited it, leaving a clear upsell and a real customer need unaddressed.
phone_presence_notes: Rance stayed polite and dropped in frequent light affirmations ('awesome,' 'no worries,' 'fantastic,' 'cool') and reacted with some empathy to Lina's situation ('Oh, wow,' 'I got you'), but leaned on 'ma'am' instead of her name for nearly the whole call and never built rapport beyond the transaction itself.
